title: Flow cytometry analysis of endothelial cells and subsets of exhausted CD8+ T cells in murine tumor models
protocol: Euthanize tumor-bearing mice by CO2 inhalation or other approved method.
Place the animal on its back on a dissection mat, pin the paws on the mat and wet the fur with 70% ethanol.
Make an incision in the abdominal area above the urethral opening without penetrating the abdominal wall and extend it until the neck using scissors.
On the tumor-bearing side of the mouse, extend the incision to hind and forelegs and pin the loose skin on the mat.
Remove fat around the tumor and take off the draining inguinal lymph node using a pair of scissors and forceps.
Delicately harvest the flank subcutaneous tumor with a scalpel ensuring that no skin is collected during the procedure.
Weigh the tumor and transfer it in a collection tube pre-filled with 1 mL Sample buffer.
Place the tube on ice and work on the next mouse.
Using scissors, mince the tumor into approximately 1-2 mm² fragments inside the collection tube.
Transfer minced tumor fragments to a digestion tube pre-filled with 1 mL Sample buffer.
Rinse twice the collection tube with 0.5 mL Sample buffer.
Obtain a final digestion volume of 3 mL.
Place the tube on ice while working on the next samples.
Prepare a digestion mix with collagenase VIII at a final concentration of 1 mg/mL and DNase I at a final concentration of 0.1 mg/mL.
Add the required volume of digestion mix to each digestion tube (2 × 30 μL = 60 μL).
Mix well in each digestion tube.
Incubate the tubes on a shaker at 180 rpm for 30 min at 37°C.
Transfer the contents of each digestion tube to individual 50 mL tubes pre-filled with 12 mL FACS buffer and overlaid with a 70 μM cell strainer.
Carefully disaggregate the remaining tumor fragments on the 70 μM strainer with a 2.5 ml syringe plunger.
Rinse the cell strainer and syringe plunger with 10 mL of FACS buffer to flush the cells through the filter.
Place the 50 mL tubes in a centrifuge and spin at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL FACS buffer.
Count total cell number in each sample using a hemocytometer or automated cell counter.
Transfer equal numbers of cells per sample to a 96-well plate.
For analysis of rare cell subsets, use a sufficient number of tumor-derived cells for flow cytometry analysis (4–8 × 10^6 cells).
Centrifuge the 96-well plate containing cells at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL of Fixable Viability Dye diluted 1:1000 in DPBS without magnesium and calcium.
Incubate the cells at 4°C for 10 min.
Discriminate live and dead cells to improve flow cytometry analysis quality.
Wash cells with 100 μL FACS buffer per well.
Centrifuge the 96-well plate at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL of antibody cocktails prepared in Staining buffer as indicated in Tables 1 and 2.
Incubate cells at 4°C for 30 min.
Wash with 100 μL FACS buffer per well.
Centrifuge the 96-well plate at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 150 μL FACS buffer and transfer to 1 mL cluster tubes pre-filled with 100 μL FACS buffer if intracellular staining is not performed.
Fix cells in 100 μL Fixation/Permeabilization solution diluted 1:3 from the Foxp3/transcription factor staining kit if intracellular staining is performed.
Incubate fixed cells at 18°C–22°C for 20 min.
Pause the experiment if fixed cells need storage, otherwise proceed immediately to washing steps.
Wash fixed cells with 100 μL FACS buffer and centrifuge the 96-well plate at 700 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant from the 96-well plate after centrifugation.
Resuspend cells in 200 μL FACS buffer.
Wash cells with 100 μL Permeabilization buffer (prepared by diluting 1:9 Permeabilization buffer 10× in distilled water) and centrifuge the 96-well plate at 700 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL of antibody cocktails (intracellular staining) prepared in Permeabilization buffer, then incubate at 4°C for 30-60 minutes.
Wash stained cells with 100 μL FACS buffer and centrifuge the 96-well plate at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend cells in 150 μL FACS buffer.
Transfer cells to 1 mL cluster tubes pre-filled with 100 μL FACS buffer.
Acquire samples on a BD LSRFortessa flow cytometer using BD FACSDiva software.
Prepare unstained control for flow cytometry.
Prepare single-stained controls for every fluorochrome used.
Set appropriate PMT voltages using unstained and single-stained controls.
Calculate auto-compensation using unstained and single-stained controls.
Define the gating strategy.
Acquire 1 × 10^6 cells per sample for rare tumor-associated endothelial cell subsets.
Acquire 0.2–0.5 × 10^6 cells per sample for tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells.
Monitor flow rate to ensure it is 8000 events/s or less during acquisition.
Identify tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells among hematopoietic CD45+ cells using the CD8a marker.
Among the identified CD8+ T cells, identify antigen-experienced exhausted CD8+ T cells as CD44+PD-1+ cells.
Further identify SLAMF6+TIM3- cells as stem-like CD8+ T cells.
Identify SLAMF6-TIM3+ cells as terminally exhausted CD8+ T cells.
Characterize stem-like and terminally exhausted CD8+ T cells with additional markers such as TCF-1 and TOX transcription factors.
